choice.ex: 밑줄 해석: 사람들이 그것을 깨닫지 못한 채 그들의 행동을 바꾸도록 만들다 해설: 노면 표시는 운전자가 '알아차리지 못한 채' 행동을 바꾸게 함 → 의식 아래에서 작용하는 신호. ②는 시각 장치라는 점은 맞지만 '강제'가 너지와 반대, ③ 은 안전이라는 목적은 맞지만 '신중한(의식적) 선택'이 without realizing it과 반대, ④는 '의도를 이해한 후'로 무의식성을 뒤집음, ⑤는 착시라는 점만 취해 '통 제력 상실'로 과장. ① 엄격한 시각적 경고를 통해 운전자들이 교통 법규를 따르도록 강제하다 ② 운전자들에게 위험을 분명히 알려 그들이 신중한 선택을 하게 하다 ③ 사람들이 설계자의 의도를 이해한 후에야 그들의 습관을 바꾸다 ④ 운전자들을 너무 혼란스럽게 해서 그들이 차량의 통제력을 잃게 하다 ⑤ 의식적인 인식 아래에서 작용하는 신호를 통해 사람들이 행동하는 방식을 형성하다

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: (A) conformity — (B) spotlights — (C) reshape
(A) conformity — (B) disguises — (C) reshape
(A) autonomy — (B) disguises — (C) restrict
(A) autonomy — (B) spotlights — (C) reshape
(A) conformity — (B) spotlights — (C) restrict
choice.ex: (A) conformity (B) spotlights (C) reshape 근거 ❷❸❹❺ 해설: (A) ❷ go along, ❺ match their behavior with that of the majority = 사회적 순응 / (B) ❸ Highlighting = 부각하다 / (C) ❹ 벌금 표지판(push) 과 달리 nudge는 선택지를 막지 않고 행동을 바꿈 = reshape. autonomy(자율성)는 다수를 따르는 성향과 반대, disguises(감추다)는 highlight와 반대, restrict(제한하다)는 선택지를 금지하지 않는 너지의 성격과 맞지 않는 함정. 요약문 해석: 사회적 (A) 순응을 향한 우리의 성향 때문에, 사람들은 완전히 납득하지 않았을 때에도 종종 다수의 행동을 받아들인다. 따라서 다른 사람들의 바람 직한 행동을 그저 (B) 부각하는 메시지는 처벌에 의존하는 메시지보다 더 미묘하게 행동을 (C) 바꿀 수 있다.
choice.psg: ❶ If you are told what other people do, you might do it too, because you think it is probably a good idea to do what they do. ❷ And even if you aren’t sure, you might not want to disobey social norms, so you will go along. ❸ Highlighting the right decisions of others can lead one to do the right thing. ❹ While the sign saying “Take your trash home or get a $100 fine.” pushes people, the one saying “Take your trash home. Other people do.” nudges them. ❺ Many people feel compelled to match their behavior with that of the majority. ❻ The decision is theirs, but they have been nudged. ❼ However, nudging people into making good choices does not always go as planned. ❽ For instance, in a study of household energy conservation, the researchers provided the residents with information about their neighbors’ average energy use. ❾ As expected, those who had consumed more energy than the average reduced their use later; however, households with low levels of energy consumption increased their use after learning that their consumption had been lower than their neighbors’. ❿ The researchers inferred that the lack of a reminder about the environmental benefits of saving energy could have caused the information to have an opposite effect. ⓫ Later, they added a smiley face to the information sent to those who used less energy than the average, and found that it neutralized the opposite effect.
choice.body: Because of our inclination toward social (A)________, people often adopt the majority’s behavior even when they are not fully convinced. Hence, a message that merely (B)________ others’ desirable conduct can (C)________ behavior more subtly than one that relies on punishment.

choice.stem: 위 글의 내용으로부터 추론할 수 없는 것을 고르시오.

choice.ex: ❾ 사용량이 적은 가정이 소비를 늘린 것은 사실이지만, ❿ 조사원들은 그 원인을 '환경적 이점을 상기시키지 않은 것'으로 추론했을 뿐 비교에 대한 분개(감정적 반발)는 언급하지 않음 — 그럴듯한 과잉 추론. 나머지는 ❶❷ / ❹ / ❾ / ❿에서 추론 가능. ① 근거 ❿ — 조사원들의 견해로는, 절약이 왜 지구에 이로운지 상기시켰다면 그 반등을 막을 수 있었을지도 모른다. ② 근거 ❾ — 같은 비교 자료가 서로 다른 가정 집단들이 반대 방향으로 행동을 바꾸게 만들 수 있다. ③ 근거 ❶❷ — 사회적 신호는 무엇이 적절한지에 대한 자신의 판단에 확신이 없는 사람들을 흔들 수 있다. ④ 근거 없음(정답) — 사용량이 적은 가정들은 자신들의 에너지 습관이 다른 사람들의 것과 비교되는 데 분개했기 때문에 소비를 늘렸다. ⑤ 근거 ❹ — 또래의 행동에 호소하는 표지판은 처벌의 위협이 아니라 사회적 영향력에 의존한다.

choice.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: people conform because they are certain the group’s choice is the most rational
uncertainty usually leads people to reject the majority and act independently
social norms are enforced mainly through fines and other formal penalties
people follow social norms only after carefully confirming that those norms are correct
people may follow a group out of reluctance to break shared expectations, not out of conviction
choice.ex: 밑줄 해석: 여러분은 사회적 규범을 어기고 싶지 않을 수도 있어서, 따르게 될 것이다 해설: ❷ even if you aren’t sure(확신이 없어도) + not want to disobey social norms(규범을 어기기 싫어서) → 확신이 아니라 규범 이탈을 꺼리는 마음 때문에 따른다는 뜻. ②는 '확인 후에야'로 조건을 뒤집음, ③은 ❹ 벌금 표지판(push)을 끌어온 부분 진실, ④는 반대, ⑤는 ❶의 이유(좋은 생각일 것)만 보고 '확신'으로 과장 — ❷의 aren’t sure와 충돌. ① 사람들은 집단의 선택이 가장 합리적이라고 확신하기 때문에 순응한다 ② 불확실성은 대개 사람들이 다수를 거부하고 독립적으로 행동하게 만든다 ③ 사회적 규범은 주로 벌금과 다른 공식적 처벌을 통해 강제된다 ④ 사람들은 사회적 규범이 옳다는 것을 신중하게 확인한 후에야 그것을 따른다 ⑤ 사람들은 확신 때문이 아니라 공유된 기대를 깨기를 꺼려서 집단을 따를 수 있다
choice.body: If you are told what other people do, you might do it too, because you think it is probably a good idea to do what they do. And even if you aren’t sure, you might not want to disobey social norms, so you will go along. Highlighting the right decisions of others can lead one to do the right thing.
choice.ul: you might not want to disobey social norms, so you will go along.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: (A) withdraw from — (B) restlessness — (C) tacit
(A) comply with — (B) restlessness — (C) explicit
(A) comply with — (B) inertia — (C) tacit
(A) withdraw from — (B) inertia — (C) tacit
(A) withdraw from — (B) inertia — (C) explicit
choice.ex: (A) withdraw from (B) inertia (C) tacit 근거 ❷❹❺ 해설: (A) ❷ opt out of the default = 디폴트에서 빠져나오다(withdraw from) / (B) ❹ a powerful desire to stick with what they already have = 현 재 상태를 유지하려는 타성(inertia) / (C) ❺ gives the impression that someone is recommending = 실제로 말하지 않았지만 '인상'으로 전해지는 암묵 적(tacit) 지지. comply with(따르다)는 이미 적용 중인 디폴트를 '따를 권리'가 되어 although 양보 구조와 맞지 않음, restlessness(변화를 원하는 들썩임) 는 ❹와 반대, explicit(명시적인)은 누군가 직접 추천한 것이 아니라 그런 '인상'을 줄 뿐이라는 ❺의 뉘앙스와 어긋나는 근접 오답. 요약문 해석: 디폴트는 능동적인 결정이 내려지지 않을 때 효력이 발생하며, 개인은 그것에서 (A) 빠져나올 권리를 유지하지만 디폴트는 확실하게 행동을 바꾼 다. 두 가지 힘이 이를 설명하는데, 바꾸는 것을 대가가 큰 일로 느끼게 하는 뿌리 깊은 (B) 타성, 그리고 사람들이 미리 설정된 선택지에서 읽어 내는 (C) 암묵적 인 지지로, 이것이 이탈을 시민으로서의 실패처럼 느끼게 만든다.
choice.psg: ❶ A default is defined as an option that applies if the chooser does nothing. ❷ Of course, the chooser has the freedom to opt out of the default. ❸ Defaults are effective at nudging people toward more desirable behaviors. ❹ Human beings are subject to a powerful desire to stick with what they already have because making a change requires a conscious effort. ❺ Furthermore, because a default also gives the impression that someone is recommending this choice, if people choose to opt out, they might feel they are not being good citizens, particularly in the case of green defaults. ❻ Setting greener choices as defaults can automatically nudge people into more sustainable behaviors. ❼ In 2008, Rutgers University instituted a new student printing policy to save on paper waste: it established printing on both sides of paper as the default setting for all its printers. ❽ As a result of that simple change, the university saved about 62 million sheets of paper in about three years.
choice.body: A default takes effect when no active decision is made, and although individuals retain the right to (A)________ it, defaults reliably shift conduct. Two forces explain this: a deep-rooted (B)________ that makes switching feel costly, and the (C)________ endorsement people read into a preset option, which makes deviating feel like a civic failing.

read.ko: 모녀 사이인 두 예술가가 인도 아메다바드의 여러 도로에 3차원 횡단보도를 그렸다.
read.en: Two artists, mother and daughter, painted a 3D crosswalk on several roads in Ahmedabad, India.

read.ko: 이렇게 그려진 선들은 운전자들에게 노상 장애물처럼 보여 너무 급작스럽게 브레이크를 밟지 않고 속도를 줄이게 만들었다.
read.en: To motorists, the painted lines look like roadblocks, causing them to slow down without braking too suddenly.

read.ko: 이 계획은 인도의 델리에서도 채택되었다.
read.en: The scheme was also adopted in Delhi, India.

read.ko: 이는 결국, 아이슬란드의 환경 위원 Ralf Trylla에게 영감을 주어 비슷한 사업을 이끌게 했다.
read.en: This, in turn, inspired Ralf Trylla, an environmental commissioner in Iceland, to head a similar project.

read.ko: 그 결과, 운전자들은 교차로에서 더 조심하게 되었고, 사고가 줄어들면서 보행자의 안전은 향상되었다.
read.en: As a result, drivers were being more careful at intersections, which reduced accidents and elevated the safety of pedestrians.

read.ko: 이 아이디어는 중국, 미국, 캐나다, 영국의 여러 도시에서도 좋은 반응을 얻고 반영되었다.
read.en: The idea has been well received and mirrored in cities of China, the U.S., Canada, and the UK as well.

read.ko: 마찬가지로, 교통 공학 전문가들은 사람들이 인식하지 못한 채 자신의 행동을 변화시키도록 하는 도로상의 노면 표시를 설계한다.
read.en: Likewise, traffic engineers design pavement markings on the roads that drive people to change their behavior without realizing it.

read.ko: 시카고는 미국에서 이 아이디어를 가장 먼저 실험한 도시 중 하나였다.
read.en: Chicago was one of the first U.S. cities to experiment with this idea.

read.ko: 2006년, 시카고는 North Lake Shore Drive의 위험한 커브 길 앞의 도로에 일련의 선들을 그렸다.
read.en: In 2006, it painted a series of lines across the road ahead of a dangerous curve on North Lake Shore Drive.

read.ko: 선들은 도로가 커브 길에 가까워질수록 그 사이 간격이 점점 더 좁아지게 되어 있다.
read.en: The lines are spaced in such a way that as the road nears the curve, the gaps between the lines get smaller and smaller.

read.ko: 이것은 커브 길에 접근하는 운전자들에게 속도를 내고 있다는 착각을 주고, 그것은 그들이 브레이크를 밟도록 유도한다.
read.en: This gives drivers approaching the curve an illusion that they are speeding up, which prompts them to step on the brakes.

read.ko: 시카고의 교통 공학 전문가들은 이 선들을 그린 후 첫 6개월 동안 North Lake Shore Drive의 커브 길에서 추돌 사고가 36% 감소했다고 보고했다.
read.en: Chicago traffic engineers reported a 36% reduction in crashes at the North Lake Shore Drive curve in the first six months after painting the lines.

read.ko: 그 후, 시카고 교통부는 유사한 커브 길에 간격을 둔 선들을 그렸다.
read.en: Since then, the Chicago Department of Transportation has painted the gapped lines at similar curves.

read.ko: 다른 사람들이 무엇을 하는지 듣게 되면, 여러분도 그들이 하는 것이 아마 좋은 생각일 것이라 여기기 때문에 똑같이 하게 될 수 있다.
read.en: If you are told what other people do, you might do it too, because you think it is probably a good idea to do what they do.

read.ko: 확신이 없더라도, 사회적 규범을 어기고 싶지 않기 때문에 따르게 된다.
read.en: And even if you aren’t sure, you might not want to disobey social norms, so you will go along.

read.ko: 타인의 올바른 결정을 강조하는 것은 개인이 올바른 행위를 하도록 이끌 수 있다.
read.en: Highlighting the right decisions of others can lead one to do the right thing.

read.ko: “쓰레기를 집으로 가져가지 않으면 100달러의 벌금을 부과합니다.”라고 쓰인 표지판이 사람들을 압박하는 것이라면, “쓰레기를 집으로 가져가세요. 다른 사람 들은 그렇게 합니다.”라고 되어 있는 표지판은 슬쩍 찌르는 것이다.
read.en: While the sign saying “Take your trash home or get a $100 fine.” pushes people, the one saying “Take your trash home. Other people do.” nudges them.

read.ko: 많은 사람들이 자신의 행동을 대다수의 행동에 맞출 것을 강요받는 기분을 느낀다.
read.en: Many people feel compelled to match their behavior with that of the majority.

read.ko: 자신이 내린 결정이지만 사실은 살며시 영향을 받은 것이다.
read.en: The decision is theirs, but they have been nudged.

read.ko: 하지만 너지로 사람들이 좋은 선택을 하도록 만드는 것이 반드시 계획대로 되지는 않는다.
read.en: However, nudging people into making good choices does not always go as planned.

read.ko: 예를 들어 가정의 에너지 절약에 대한 연구에서 조사원들은 주민들에게 이웃들의 평균 에너지 사용량에 대한 정보를 제공했다.
read.en: For instance, in a study of household energy conservation, the researchers provided the residents with information about their neighbors’ average energy use.

read.ko: 예상대로, 평균보다 더 많은 에너지를 소비한 가정은 이후 사용량을 줄였지만, 에너지 소비 정도가 낮은 가정은 이웃보다 소비량이 낮다는 것을 알고 나서 에너 지 사용량을 늘렸다.
read.en: As expected, those who had consumed more energy than the average reduced their use later; however, households with low levels of energy consumption increased their use after learning that their consumption had been lower than their neighbors’.

read.ko: 조사원들은 에너지 절감의 환경 편익을 상기시키지 않은 것이 해당 정보의 역효과를 초래했다고 추론했다.
read.en: The researchers inferred that the lack of a reminder about the environmental benefits of saving energy could have caused the information to have an opposite effect.

read.ko: 이후, 그들은 평균보다 에너지를 적게 쓰는 가정에게 보내는 정보에 웃는 얼굴 이모티콘을 추가했고, 그것이 그 역효과를 상쇄했음을 발견했다.
read.en: Later, they added a smiley face to the information sent to those who used less energy than the average, and found that it neutralized the opposite effect.

read.ko: 디폴트는 선택하는 사람이 아무것도 하지 않을 경우 적용되는 선택지라고 정의된다.
read.en: A default is defined as an option that applies if the chooser does nothing.

read.ko: 물론 선택하는 사람은 디폴트에서 빠져나올 자유가 있다.
read.en: Of course, the chooser has the freedom to opt out of the default.

read.ko: 디폴트는 사람들을 보다 바람직한 행동 쪽으로 유도하는 데 효과적이다.
read.en: Defaults are effective at nudging people toward more desirable behaviors.

read.ko: 인간은 이미 갖고 있는 것을 고수하려는 강력한 성향이 있는데, 변화하는 것은 의식적인 노력이 필요하기 때문이다.
read.en: Human beings are subject to a powerful desire to stick with what they already have because making a change requires a conscious effort.

read.ko: 게다가 디폴트는 누군가가 해당 선택지를 추천한다는 인상을 주기 때문에, 특히 환경친화적 디폴트의 경우, 이와 다른 선택을 할 경우 올바른 시민처럼 행동하고 있지 않다고 느낄 수 있다.
read.en: Furthermore, because a default also gives the impression that someone is recommending this choice, if people choose to opt out, they might feel they are not being good citizens, particularly in the case of green defaults.

read.ko: 환경친화적 선택을 디폴트로 두는 것은 사람들을 보다 지속 가능한 행동으로 자연스럽게 이끌 수 있다.
read.en: Setting greener choices as defaults can automatically nudge people into more sustainable behaviors.

read.ko: 2008년 Rutgers 대학은 종이 낭비를 줄이기 위해 새로운 학생 출력 정책을 시행했는데, 모든 출력 장치에서 양면 출력을 디폴트 설정으로 지정한 것이었다.
read.en: In 2008, Rutgers University instituted a new student printing policy to save on paper waste: it established printing on both sides of paper as the default setting for all its printers.

read.ko: 이 간단한 변화의 결과로 대학은 약 3년 동안 6천 2백만 장의 종이를 절약했다.
read.en: As a result of that simple change, the university saved about 62 million sheets of paper in about three years.

read.ko: 디폴트를 활용한 너지는 음식 배달 앱에도 적용할 수 있다.
read.en: Nudging through defaults can also apply to a food delivery app.

read.ko: 최근 한 업체는 포크, 숟가락, 빨대와 같은 선택 품목의 디폴트 설정을 바꾸는 앱 업데이트를 발표했다.
read.en: A company recently announced an update for its app where it would change the default settings for the optional items, such as forks, spoons, and straws.

read.ko: 이 품목들을 받으려면 사용자가 디폴트 설정을 변경해야 한다.
read.en: Users would have to opt out of the default to get them.

read.ko: 해당 업체는 많은 고객들을 상대로 설문 조사를 실시한 결과, 90% 이상이 주문할 때 실제로는 일회용 플라스틱 제품이 필요하지 않다고 한 것을 발견했다고 온 라인 게시물을 통해 밝혔다.
read.en: The company mentioned in an online post that having surveyed many of its customers, they found that more than 90% of them didn’t really need disposable plastic items with their orders.

read.ko: 사람들의 특정 행동을 변화시키는 데 관심이 있는가?
read.en: Are you interested in changing certain people’s behavior?

read.ko: 그렇다면 올바른 방향으로 이들을 넌지시 유도해 보는 것은 어떨까?
read.en: Then why not nudge them in the right direction?

read.ko: 사람들이 더 나은 결정을 내리도록 미묘하게 영향을 주는 방법은 많다.
read.en: There are many ways to subtly influence people to make better decisions.

read.ko: 우리 모두가 때때로 선택 설계자이기 때문에, 사람들을 올바른 길에 놓는 방법을 아는 것은 도움이 된다.
read.en: As we are all choice architects every now and then, it pays to know how to set people on the right path.

para.en: You have probably received a notification from your smartphone telling you that it is time to exercise or move. These devices lead people to move by sending notifications when they have been inactive for a set amount of time. You may not have realized it, but this is an example of a nudge. A nudge is an intervention that gently guides individuals toward a desired action, without forbidding any options. For example, if a school wants to reduce the amount of sugary drinks that students consume, then making them less visible than bottled water counts as a nudge, while banning them altogether does not. Having been studied in the domain of behavioral economics and marketing, nudging can be applied to inducing people to make better or ideal decisions. Here are some ways nudges have succeeded in bringing about positive changes by tweaking people’s choices.

Changes in visual designs can markedly affect behaviors of people, especially on streets. Two artists, mother and daughter, painted a 3D crosswalk on several roads in Ahmedabad, India. To motorists, the painted lines look like roadblocks, causing them to slow down without braking too suddenly. The scheme was also adopted in Delhi, India. This, in turn, inspired Ralf Trylla, an environmental commissioner in Iceland, to head a similar project. As a result, drivers were being more careful at intersections, which reduced accidents and elevated the safety of pedestrians. The idea has been well received and mirrored in cities of China, the U.S., Canada, and the UK as well. Likewise, traffic engineers design pavement markings on the roads that drive people to change their behavior without realizing it. Chicago was one of the first U.S. cities to experiment with this idea. In 2006, it painted a series of lines across the road ahead of a dangerous curve on North Lake Shore Drive. The lines are spaced in such a way that as the road nears the curve, the gaps between the lines get smaller and smaller. This gives drivers approaching the curve an illusion that they are speeding up, which prompts them to step on the brakes. Chicago traffic engineers reported a 36% reduction in crashes at the North Lake Shore Drive curve in the first six months after painting the lines. Since then, the Chicago Department of Transportation has painted the gapped lines at similar curves.

If you are told what other people do, you might do it too, because you think it is probably a good idea to do what they do. And even if you aren’t sure, you might not want to disobey social norms, so you will go along. Highlighting the right decisions of others can lead one to do the right thing. While the sign saying “Take your trash home or get a $100 fine.” pushes people, the one saying “Take your trash home. Other people do.” nudges them. Many people feel compelled to match their behavior with that of the majority. The decision is theirs, but they have been nudged. However, nudging people into making good choices does not always go as planned. For instance, in a study of household energy conservation, the researchers provided the residents with information about their neighbors’ average energy use. As expected, those who had consumed more energy than the average reduced their use later; however, households with low levels of energy consumption increased their use after learning that their consumption had been lower than their neighbors’. The researchers inferred that the lack of a reminder about the environmental benefits of saving energy could have caused the information to have an opposite effect. Later, they added a smiley face to the information sent to those who used less energy than the average, and found that it neutralized the opposite effect.

A default is defined as an option that applies if the chooser does nothing. Of course, the chooser has the freedom to opt out of the default. Defaults are effective at nudging people toward more desirable behaviors. Human beings are subject to a powerful desire to stick with what they already have because making a change requires a conscious effort. Furthermore, because a default also gives the impression that someone is recommending this choice, if people choose to opt out, they might feel they are not being good citizens, particularly in the case of green defaults. Setting greener choices as defaults can automatically nudge people into more sustainable behaviors. In 2008, Rutgers University instituted a new student printing policy to save on paper waste: it established printing on both sides of paper as the default setting for all its printers. As a result of that simple change, the university saved about 62 million sheets of paper in about three years.

Nudging through defaults can also apply to a food delivery app. A company recently announced an update for its app where it would change the default settings for the optional items, such as forks, spoons, and straws. Users would have to opt out of the default to get them. The company mentioned in an online post that having surveyed many of its customers, they found that more than 90% of them didn’t really need disposable plastic items with their orders. Are you interested in changing certain people’s behavior? Then why not nudge them in the right direction? There are many ways to subtly influence people to make better decisions. As we are all choice architects every now and then, it pays to know how to set people on the right path.
